solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: However made, a TV programme easy to dip in and out of (2,2,5)

indicators: to dip in and out of

indicatorNotes.to dip in and out of: dipping in and out of a word means touching one letter, skipping the next, touching the one after

blocks.clueFragment: easy to dip in and out of
blocks.note: E and S, the first and third letters of EaSy

annotation.surface: A TV guide praising a show you can watch any episode of without losing the thread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'However made' reads like the start of a TV review, but it is the definition: an order taken 'as it comes' is accepted however it happens to be made.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from ordering drinks: whisky or coffee 'as it comes' is served however it is made, with no special instructions.

entries.clue: It sets like a shot (5)

blocks.note: a pic is a photo, a shot

annotation.surface: Something that sets instantly, quick as a gunshot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Like a shot' is an idiom for 'instantly', so the surface says the thing sets fast; the solver has to break the idiom into two separate words.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: aspic is a savoury jelly, and setting is what jelly does.

entries.clue: Finally hotel-resistant, staggering around end of tour (2,3,4,6)

indicatorNotes.staggering: someone staggering lurches about unsteadily, as these letters do out of their order
indicatorNotes.around: the jumbled letters sit around the extra R, taking it in among them
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter, here the R of 'tour'

blocks.note: last letter of touR, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A tourist ending a tour by staggering about, finally refusing to go back to the hotel.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram needs one more letter than 'hotel-resistant' supplies; the R from the end of 'tour' is the letter the others stagger around.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'in the last resort' means when all else has failed, so finally.

entries.clue: Herald’s lying in grass with a collection of books (8)

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

annotation.surface: A herald lounging on the lawn with a pile of books.
annotation.walkthrough: In the surface the apostrophe-s means 'is'; for the definition it is possessive: the herald's word for 'lying'.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: in heraldry, a beast shown lying down with its head raised is described as couchant.

entries.clue: Egotist’s urgent claim that spreads online (4)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for 'something that spreads online'

blocks.note: the egotist's favourite word, about themself
the same word said again, urgently, to claim attention

annotation.surface: A self-obsessed person's demands going viral.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Me! Me!' is the egotist's urgent cry. 'Claim' does double duty, as the egotist's demand and as the kind of assertion that gets passed around the internet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by behaviour: a meme is an image, joke or idea that users copy and pass on until it has spread across the internet.

entries.clue: Boor reacts furiously — language! (5-5)

indicatorNotes.furiously: a furious reaction flails wildly, throwing the letters out of order

annotation.surface: A lout loses his temper, and someone scolds him for his swearing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Language!' is what you snap at someone swearing, so it hides as a reprimand rather than a definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Serbo-Croat is the South Slavic language spoken in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro.

entries.clue: Carried on getting regular money (5)

blocks.note: as in carried on a war or a campaign

annotation.surface: Someone kept going because a salary kept coming in.
annotation.walkthrough: One word doing two jobs: a past-tense verb (to wage war) and an adjective (the waged, as against the unwaged).
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain synonyms: to wage a war is to carry it on, and the waged are those drawing a regular pay packet.

entries.clue: Exhausted fiancée stops scheming like some women (6)

indicatorNotes.Exhausted: something exhausted has been emptied out, so the word keeps only its shell of outer letters
indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a hole is to plug it, so the FE plugs the middle of WILY

blocks.note: FiancéE with its middle emptied out

annotation.surface: A worn-out bride-to-be gives up her plotting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'stops' mean 'gives up'; it is the plugging sense. The accent on fiancée is irrelevant, since only its first and last letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: wifely means befitting a wife, and wives are some women.

entries.clue: Dropping arms, she strangely exhibits small attention span (11,4)

indicatorNotes.strangely: letters arranged strangely are in an odd, unfamiliar order

annotation.surface: A woman lets her arms fall and seems unable to concentrate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a verb acting on 'arms', as if letters were to be removed; it is simply fodder, and every letter of the first three words is used.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a grasshopper mind jumps from topic to topic like the insect, which is a short attention span.

entries.clue: Splitting up, speak rudely to individual not working (9)

indicatorNotes.not working: a machine that is working is on, so 'not working' asks for ON to be removed

blocks.note: to dis someone is to speak disrespectfully of them

annotation.surface: A couple breaking up, one insulting the other for being out of work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speak rudely to' reads as one verb phrase; the 'to' is only glue. The deletion takes ON out of the middle of PERSONAL, not off the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: a crowd's splitting up and scattering is its dispersal.

entries.clue: Novel way to prepare extending the patio? (3,3,4,5)

annotation.definition: Novel way to prepare extending the patio?

blocks.note: the surface reads 'new'; the setter means a book, a novel

blocks.clueFragment: way to prepare extending the patio?
blocks.note: flags are paving flagstones, not banners: laying more of them makes a patio bigger

annotation.surface: A new method for getting ready to enlarge a garden terrace.
annotation.walkthrough: Put Out More Flags is Evelyn Waugh's 1942 novel. Read literally, its title is an instruction to lay more paving stones.
annotation.definitionFit: The title's words, taken at face value, describe setting out extra flagstones, which is how you extend a patio.

entries.clue: Babies here in playground wearing red (6)

annotation.definitionNote: a place clued by what is found there

indicatorNotes.wearing: a garment being worn wraps round its wearer, so CHE is put round REC

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the archetypal red revolutionary
the rec, short for recreation ground

annotation.surface: Toddlers in a playground dressed in red.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the playground wearing red; the wordplay puts the red round the playground. 'Red' looks like a colour but is a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by contents: a crèche is a nursery, the place where babies are looked after.

entries.clue: Two sources of energy containing key blend (8)

indicatorNotes.containing: to contain something is to hold it inside, as COAL…E holds ESC

blocks.note: COAL, and E, the physics symbol for energy
the Esc key on a keyboard

annotation.surface: A mix of two power sources, with something key in the middle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' wants to be an adjective or a musical key; it is the escape key on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: things that coalesce blend and merge into one.

entries.clue: Don’t go near ox, plainly (5,5)

blocks.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
clear as an adverb, as in 'loud and clear'

annotation.surface: A plain warning to keep away from an ox.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a farmyard warning that means exactly what the answer means, so the definition hardly hides.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from navigation: to steer clear of something is to keep well away from it.

entries.clue: Her actions damaged one of several branches (5,5)

indicatorNotes.damaged: something damaged is knocked out of shape, as these letters are

annotation.surface: Someone's behaviour broke off part of a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests a tree her actions harmed; they are shops of one retailer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: each outlet of a retail chain is one branch among many.

entries.clue: Pale actor transformed her death scene? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is the queen; the definition names her by her most famous scene

indicatorNotes.transformed: to transform something is to change its form, here the order of the letters

annotation.surface: A pallid actress changing for her big death scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an indirect definition: 'her' is the woman whose death by asp bite is among the most famous on stage.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by allusion: the asp-bite suicide ending Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra is her death scene.

entries.clue: School leaving German castle in deficit (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: to leave a place is to go out of it, so SCH goes out of SCHLOSS

blocks.note: sch is the standard abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: A school pulls out of a German castle trip that ran at a loss.
annotation.walkthrough: Even without German, the abbreviation SCH for school shows where the deletion starts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from accounts: a business running at a loss is in deficit.

entries.clue: Cooking Italian brought up to eat with old men (8)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, bringing something up lifts it from bottom to top, so the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.to eat: what eats takes the food inside it, so TI takes AND O OR inside

blocks.note: It. is the abbreviation for Italian
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: An Italian chef invited to dinner with a group of old men.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' looks like what the Italian is doing; it is the definition, as in a style of cooking.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: tandoori is a style of Indian cooking done in a clay oven, the tandoor.

entries.clue: Takes on board chairs, not the first (4)

indicatorNotes.not the first: the word is taken without its first letter, which is not included

annotation.surface: A board meeting where the one who takes the chair is not the first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Takes on board' suggests understanding an idea; here it is food being taken on board.
annotation.definitionFit: A jokey idiom: taking food on board means eating it.

entries.clue: Visited a fellow motoring enthusiast to give a bit of a hand (10)

blocks.note: met = visited, as in met with
a PAL (fellow) whose passion is the CAR

annotation.surface: Dropping in on a fellow car enthusiast to help out with some work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give a hand' promises help; the definition is literally a part of the hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by part: the metacarpals are the five bones of the palm, each a bit of the hand.

entries.clue: Leg after end of swim, one still glowing (6)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter, here the M of 'swim'
indicatorNotes.after: coming after means following in order, so EMBER is placed behind the M

blocks.note: an ember is a piece of a dying fire still glowing

annotation.surface: A swimmer's leg, still glowing after the final length.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' does not mean the leg comes after the swim; it tells you the glowing piece follows the letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a leg is a limb, and member is a formal word for a limb.

entries.clue: Authoritative impression of reserve with a little money around (8)

indicatorNotes.around: something placed around another surrounds it, so PENCE surrounds RES

blocks.note: a few pence is a small sum
res is the abbreviation for reserve

annotation.surface: A reserved person who gives an impression of authority despite having little money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a personality trait belonging with 'impression'; it is only the abbreviation RES.
annotation.definitionFit: A particular sense: someone with presence makes a commanding impression just by being in the room.

entries.clue: Bother sailors beginning to swab decks (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here the S of 'swab'

annotation.surface: Sailors are made to begin swabbing the ship's decks.
annotation.walkthrough: With 'sailors' and 'swab' around it, 'decks' reads as the floors of a ship; it is the verb, as in 'deck the halls'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to deck a room with holly is to adorn it.

entries.clue: Source of sweetness in sauces from the south (5)

indicatorNotes.from the south: in a down clue, reading from the south means starting at the bottom and reading upwards

annotation.surface: Looking for what makes Southern cooking sauces so sweet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From the south' sounds like regional cooking, but in a down clue it says the word runs bottom to top.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: sugar is the everyday ingredient added to make food sweet.

entries.clue: Fancy wife being supported by that man (4)

indicatorNotes.being supported by: in a down clue, what is supported rests on top, so W sits above HIM

annotation.surface: A wife likes the idea of being kept by her man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb (the wife fancies being kept); it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: a passing fancy is a sudden, idle notion.

entries.clue: Sorting out problems with noise in parliament? (15)

blocks.note: a parliament is the collective noun for owls, and this is the noise they make

annotation.surface: Dealing with the problem of rowdy MPs shouting in the chamber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parliament' wants to be Westminster; the question mark hints at a parliament of owls. 'Problems' belongs to the wordplay, although 'sorting out problems' reads as one phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A particular sense: troubleshooting is tracing and sorting out faults, especially in machines or systems.

entries.clue: A prison is busy (5)

blocks.note: stir is old slang for prison

annotation.surface: A jail is a hive of activity.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a complete sentence; the definition is its last word and 'is' joins the two halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both adjectives: a household astir is up and moving about, busy.

entries.clue: Several weeks in Provence introduced to provide rest (9)

indicatorNotes.introduced to: to introduce something is to put it in, so MAI goes into RENDER

blocks.note: to render a service is to provide it
Mai is French for May, a month of several weeks

annotation.surface: A few weeks in the south of France as a well-earned break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In Provence' means 'in French', so the several weeks are a French month; 'rest' looks like a holiday and means what is left over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns: the rest of something is what is left, its remainder.
